title: A Culture of Secrecy That Perpetuated Abuse

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我负责《纽约时报》每日新闻简报 DealBook 的商业与政策报道。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市 DealBook 峰会的现场，采访商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的几位领袖，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde,
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、

sentences.en: Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经滤镜的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch, free, at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 我们将在 11 月 18 日在 nytimes.com 上免费直播部分精选采访，供所有人观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序来观看，并获得我们所有新闻报道的一个月免费体验权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今天是。

sentences.en: A grand jury report finds that Catholic priests abused 1,000 children in Pennsylvania over a period of 70 years.
sentences.zh: 一份大陪审团报告发现，在 70 年的时间里，宾夕法尼亚州的的天主教神父虐待了 1,000 名儿童。

sentences.en: The church insists it's old news, but details of the report suggest it's not.
sentences.zh: 教会坚称这已经是陈旧的旧闻，但报告的细节表明并非如此。

sentences.en: It's Thursday, August 16th.
sentences.zh: 今天是 8 月 16 日，星期四。

sentences.en: Lori Goodstein, this feels like the most explosive reporting on the Catholic Church since the Boston Globe's spotlight reporting 16 years ago.
sentences.zh: 洛里·古德斯坦，这感觉像是自 16 年前《波士顿环球报》的聚焦报道以来，关于天主教教会最具爆炸性的报道。

sentences.en: Did it come as a surprise to you as a religion reporter?
sentences.zh: 作为一名宗教记者，你对此感到意外吗？

sentences.en: I have to say it didn't.
sentences.zh: 我必须说，我并不意外。

sentences.en: We are now in a new stage of the clergy sex abuse scandal in the Catholic Church,
sentences.zh: 我们现在正处于天主教教会神职人员性虐待丑闻的新阶段，

sentences.en: and things had been kind of revving up even before this Pennsylvania grand jury report was released.
sentences.zh: 甚至在这份宾夕法尼亚州大陪审团报告发布之前，事态就已经在某种程度上加速升温了。

sentences.en: Lori Goodstein covers religion for The Times.
sentences.zh: 洛里·古德斯坦为《时报》报道宗教新闻。

sentences.en: A lot of Catholics were asking, what did people in the hierarchy know about a particular cardinal?
sentences.zh: 许多天主教徒都在问：教会高层对某位特定的红衣主教了解多少？

sentences.en: That's Theodore McCarrick, who was the former Archbishop of Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: 那个人就是西奥多·麦卡里克，他曾任华盛顿特区大主教。

sentences.en: And he resigned very recently because he had a record of abusing not only children, but also seminarians and young priests.
sentences.zh: 他最近辞职了，因为他不仅有虐待儿童的记录，还有虐待修道生和年轻神父的记录。

sentences.en: And apparently warnings about him were made to Catholic officials, to his brother bishops, to Vatican officials in the United States, and likely to the Vatican in Rome as well.
sentences.zh: 显然，有关他的警告曾被传达给天主教官员、同僚主教、美国梵蒂冈官员，很可能也传达到了罗马的梵蒂冈。

sentences.en: And not only was he kept in place over many years, but he was made a cardinal and given a very prominent seat in Washington.
sentences.zh: 不仅他多年来一直稳坐高位，而且他还被册封为红衣主教，并在华盛顿占据了非常显赫的席位。

sentences.en: And his resignation, McCarrick, told you what about this new stage in the church abuse scandal?
sentences.zh: 麦卡里克的辞职，向你说明了关于教会虐待丑闻这一新阶段的什么情况？

sentences.en: Well, it got people looking at systemic cover-up.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这让人们开始审视系统的包庇。

sentences.en: So now we're in a stage where the people at the very top of the church are themselves accused of being abusers.
sentences.zh: 所以现在我们处于这样一个阶段：教会最顶层的人自己也被指控为施虐者。

sentences.en: And you're looking at the people around them and asking, what did they know?
sentences.zh: 而你看着他们周围的人，并质问：他们知道些什么？

sentences.en: When did they know it?
sentences.zh: 他们是什么时候知道的？

sentences.en: So what exactly is in this report that was handed down by this grand jury in Pennsylvania on Tuesday?
sentences.zh: 那么，周二宾夕法尼亚州这个大陪审团发布的报告里究竟写了些什么？

sentences.en: Well, partly what you get is some numbers.
sentences.zh: 嗯，部分内容是关于一些数字。

sentences.en: It looked at six dioceses in Pennsylvania, six out of the eight dioceses in Pennsylvania,
sentences.zh: 它调查了宾夕法尼亚州的六个教区，也就是宾州八个教区中的六个，

sentences.en: and found that there were 300 priests that they could identify who were credibly accused of sexually abusing children.
sentences.zh: 并发现有 300 名他们能够确定的神父，遭到了性虐待儿童的可信指控。

sentences.en: 1,000 potential victims that they could identify.
sentences.zh: 他们能够确定的潜在受害者有 1,000 人。

sentences.en: But they very quickly said that those numbers are really a shot in the dark, that they're probably an undercount.
sentences.zh: 但他们很快就表示，这些数字其实只是凭空猜测，实际统计数字可能被低估了。

sentences.en: They say that there are victims who either are too afraid to come forward or whose abuser priests were not showing up in church files.
sentences.zh: 他们表示，有些受害者要么太害怕而不敢站出来，要么施虐神父的名字根本没有出现在教会档案中。

sentences.en: The grand jury relied, to a great extent, on the church's own files.
sentences.zh: 大陪审团在很大程度上依赖了教会自己的档案。

sentences.en: All bishops keep secret archives.
sentences.zh: 所有主教都保留着秘密档案。

sentences.en: Those were subpoenaed, and the grand jury looked at, they say, half a million pages.
sentences.zh: 这些档案被传讯了，大陪审团查阅了他们所说的大约五十万页资料。

sentences.en: And so they were pulling names and records of priests out of those documents.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们是从这些文件中提取神父的名字和记录。

sentences.en: Now, if there was a priest who didn't show up in a document, who was never known to be an abuser,
sentences.zh: 现在，如果有一个神父没有出现在文件中，从不知道是一个施虐者，

sentences.en: well, you know, those victims and that priest is not going to be counted in this report.
sentences.zh: 那么，你知道的，这些受害者和那个神父就不会被统计在这份报告中。

sentences.en: So even that set of astonishing numbers, 1,000 victims, 300 accused priests, they're basically saying, this grand jury, that that's probably a significant understatement.
sentences.zh: 因此，即使是那组惊人的数字——1,000 名受害者、300 名被指控的神父，这个大陪审团基本上是在说，这可能是一个严重的保守估计。

sentences.en: They did say that.
sentences.zh: 他们确实这么说了。

sentences.en: And I have to say that these numbers sound like a lot to a lot of people, but they don't to me.
sentences.zh: 我必须说，对很多人来说这些数字听起来很大，但对我来说并非如此。

sentences.en: We've been looking at numbers like this from other dioceses where we've been able to get a clear picture.
sentences.zh: 我们一直在关注来自其他教区的类似数字，在那些地方我们能够拼凑出清晰的全貌。

sentences.en: And there are very few.
sentences.zh: 而且这样的报告非常少。

sentences.en: I mean, there have been very few of these kinds of reports.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这类报告一直以来都非常少。

sentences.en: And the reason this one in Pennsylvania was so groundbreaking is it practically looked at an entire state.
sentences.zh: 宾夕法尼亚州这份报告之所以具有如此开创性，是因为它几乎调查了整个州。

sentences.en: It's the first time a government entity has investigated what happened in almost an entire state.
sentences.zh: 这是政府实体首次对几乎整个州内发生的事情进行调查。

sentences.en: And now the entire state of Pennsylvania actually has been studied because there were grand juries also in the other two remaining dioces,
sentences.zh: 现在，整个宾夕法尼亚州实际上都已经受到了调查，因为其余两个剩下的教区——

sentences.en: Philadelphia and the Diocese of Altoona, Johnstown.
sentences.zh: 费城和阿尔图纳-约翰斯敦教区——也设立了大陪审团。

sentences.en: So it sounds like it's actually pretty rare for an entire state to be studied this way when it comes to the church.
sentences.zh: 听起来，在教会问题上，对整个州进行这样的调查其实非常罕见。

sentences.en: It never happened before.
sentences.zh: 以前从未发生过。

sentences.en: This is unprecedented in the United States.
sentences.zh: 这在美国是史无前例的。

sentences.en: What are some of the details of the abuse that struck you in particular in this report from Pennsylvania?
sentences.zh: 在宾夕法尼亚州的这份报告中，有哪些虐待细节特别触动了你？

sentences.en: Well, I'm hesitating, I guess, because of the breadth of the depravity.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我犹豫不决，我想是因为堕落的广度。

sentences.en: I mean, I've been covering this a long time.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我报道这个已经很久了。

sentences.en: But when you see a collection of abuse like this, the vulnerability of the victiMs.
sentences.zh: 但是当你看到这样一批虐待事件时，受害者的脆弱性……

sentences.en: I mean, you know, without going into too much explicit detail, there were children abused in hospital rooMs.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道的，在不透露过多露骨细节的情况下，有儿童在病房里遭到虐待。

sentences.en: There were three sisters in one family abused, one as young as 18 months old.
sentences.zh: 有一个家庭里有三姐妹遭到虐待，其中最小的一个只有 18 个月大。

sentences.en: There were some things that read as though it was torture, children who were whipped, stripped and whipped.
sentences.zh: 有些事情读起来就像是酷刑，孩子们被鞭打，被剥光衣服然后鞭打。

sentences.en: You know, it's just a collection of horrors.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这简直是一堆恐怖事件的集合。

sentences.en: And so when you read through this thing, I mean, the grand jurors, as you read the report, you can see how appalled and angry they are.
sentences.zh: 所以当你通读这份东西时，大陪审员们——当你阅读报告时，你能看出他们是多么的震惊和愤怒。

sentences.en: They are angry about what they learned.
sentences.zh: 他们对他们所了解到的一切感到愤怒。

sentences.en: What do you mean?
sentences.zh: 你是什么意思？

sentences.en: And then as a reader, you can't help feeling that way also.
sentences.zh: 然后作为读者，你也不禁会有这种感受。

sentences.en: How could you actually see their anger in this written report?
sentences.zh: 你究竟怎么能在这份书面报告中看出他们的愤怒？

sentences.en: Well, partly it's in the choice of words.
sentences.zh: 嗯，部分体现在用词的选择上。

sentences.en: They talk in particular about a playbook for concealing the truth.
sentences.zh: 他们特别谈到了一个隐瞒真相的“战术手册”。

sentences.en: And then they go through point by point.
sentences.zh: 然后他们逐条列举。

sentences.en: Well, what does the playbook look like?
sentences.zh: 嗯，这个战术手册看起来是怎样的？

sentences.en: And the tone of it is almost sarcastic because they're talking about, well, if you were to follow a playbook, here's what you do as church officials.
sentences.zh: 它的语气几乎带有讽刺意味，因为他们在讨论：嗯，如果你要遵循一份战术手册，作为教会官员，你要这么做。

sentences.en: Number one, use euphemisMs.
sentences.zh: 第一条，使用委婉语。

sentences.en: Don't talk about rape or abuse or molestation.
sentences.zh: 不要谈论强奸、虐待或猥亵。

sentences.en: Talk about inappropriate contact.
sentences.zh: 要谈论不当接触。

sentences.en: Can you hear the sarcasm here?
sentences.zh: 你能听到这里的讽刺意味吗？

sentences.en: Number two is send only inexperienced people to conduct investigations.
sentences.zh: 第二条是只派毫无经验的人去进行调查。

sentences.en: So make it look like you're investigating, but then send people who are completely unprepared to actually judge or hear cases of child sexual abuse.
sentences.zh: 所以看起来你好像在调查，但随后派去的人完全没有准备好去真正评判或审理儿童性虐待案件。

sentences.en: Number three is then send the priest to a church-run treatment center.
sentences.zh: 第三条是把神父送到教会开办的治疗中心。

sentences.en: And then if you do remove a priest, number four, don't tell parishioners why.
sentences.zh: 然后，如果你确实免去了神父的职务，第四条，不要告诉教区居民原因。

sentences.en: You know, say he's on medical leave or, you know, he's had to take another assignment.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，就说他在休病假，或者，你知道的，他不得不接受另一项委派。

sentences.en: But don't be honeSt.
sentences.zh: 但不要说实话。

sentences.en: And then number five is continue to provide him housing and pay him a salary.
sentences.zh: 然后第五条是继续为他提供住房并向他支付薪水。

sentences.en: Even if he has committed child abuse.
sentences.zh: 即使他犯下了虐待儿童罪。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Now, number six in the playbook is if his conduct becomes known, don't remove him from the priesthood.
sentences.zh: 现在，战术手册中的第六条是，如果他的行为败露，不要开除他的神职。

sentences.en: Instead, transfer him to another parish, another location.
sentences.zh: 相反，把他调到另一个教区、另一个地方。

sentences.en: And then last, they say, above all, don't tell the police.
sentences.zh: 然后最后，他们说，最重要的是，不要告诉警察。

sentences.en: And it seems like everything about this is crafted to prevent these cases and these stories from becoming public or entering the legal system.
sentences.zh: 似乎这一切都是为了防止这些案件和故事公之于众或进入法律系统而精心设计的。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Above all, the thing guiding the bishops is prevent scandal.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，指导主教们的原则是防止丑闻。

sentences.en: Scandal could cause people to turn away from the faith.
sentences.zh: 丑闻可能会导致人们背离信仰。

sentences.en: It could cause people to turn away from the church.
sentences.zh: 它可能会导致人们背离教会。

sentences.en: So you don't want that.
sentences.zh: 所以你不希望这样。

sentences.en: And so, in some ways, they're saying, we're protecting our people from this disturbing news.
sentences.zh: 因此，在某种程度上，他们是在说，我们在保护我们的人民免受这些令人不安的消息的影响。

sentences.en: The other thing, though, that they're doing is they're protecting their priests.
sentences.zh: 不过，他们做的另一件事是保护他们的神父。

sentences.en: They're protecting the church.
sentences.zh: 他们在保护教会。

sentences.en: I mean, the irony here, of course, is that this is the worst thing that has happened to the church, you know, since the Reformation.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这里的讽刺之处当然在于，这是自宗教改革以来，教会遭遇的最糟糕的事情。

sentences.en: Historians say this.
sentences.zh: 历史学家们都这么说。

sentences.en: That's how cataclysmic this is.
sentences.zh: 这就是它的灾难性所在。

sentences.en: So they were attempting to protect the church, but it has all backfired.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们曾试图保护教会，但这一切都适得其反。

sentences.en: So is the greatest crime that this report is unearthing, not necessarily the abuse itself, as absolutely horrific as it was,
sentences.zh: 那么这份报告所挖掘出的最大罪行，不一定是虐待本身——尽管它绝对令人毛骨悚然——

sentences.en: but the systematic complicity and the kind of intentional covering up that occurred afterwards inside the church?
sentences.zh: 而是随后在教会内部发生的系统性共谋和某种蓄意掩盖吗？

sentences.en: Well, that is what a lot of abuse survivors have told me over the years.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这就是多年来许多虐待幸存者对我说的话。

sentences.en: Yes, the abuse was terrible.
sentences.zh: 是的，虐待很糟糕。

sentences.en: It was painful.
sentences.zh: 它很痛苦。

sentences.en: It's given me nightmares.
sentences.zh: 它给了我噩梦。

sentences.en: But the real torture was being turned away by my own church or not being believed.
sentences.zh: 但真正的折磨是被我自己的教会拒之门外，或者不被信任。

sentences.en: They say that has hurt a whole lot more than the initial abuse.
sentences.zh: 他们说，这比最初的虐待伤害要大得多。

sentences.en: I hear that over and over.
sentences.zh: 我一次又一次地听到这种说法。

sentences.en: It sounds like you talk to a lot of people who were abused by the Catholic Church.
sentences.zh: 听起来你采访过许多遭到天主教教会虐待的人。

sentences.en: I have.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And what's amazing is both how similar the stories sound and yet how each time someone tells me something that is so astounding that I can't get over it.
sentences.zh: 令人惊奇的是，这些故事听起来既如此相似，然而每次有人告诉我一些事情时，又是如此令人震惊，以至于我无法释怀。

sentences.en: And something like that happened reporting this last story, too.
sentences.zh: 在报道这个最新的故事时，也发生了类似的事情。

sentences.en: What was it?
sentences.zh: 是什么？

sentences.en: Well, this is a man who did testify before this grand jury, and he was abused as a child for, I think he told me, about three years, I think starting from the age of 10,
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是一个曾在这次大陪审团面前作证的男子，他小时候遭到虐待，据他告诉我，我想大约有三年时间，大概从 10 岁开始，

sentences.en: by his parish prieSt.
sentences.zh: 被他的教区神父虐待。

sentences.en: Amazingly, this man became a prieSt.
sentences.zh: 令人惊奇的是，这个人后来成了一名神父。

sentences.en: His name is James Velujak.
sentences.zh: 他的名字叫詹姆斯·韦卢雅克。

sentences.en: He told me that in 2010, he finally decided he would go and tell his bishop what happened to him as a child.
sentences.zh: 他告诉我，在 2010 年，他终于决定去告诉他的主教他在小时候遭遇了什么。

sentences.en: And he says that the bishop asked him, how many times were you abused, do you think?
sentences.zh: 他说主教问他：你觉得你被虐待了多少次？

sentences.en: And James said about 15.
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯说大约 15 次。

sentences.en: He said the bishop said to him, oh, you were lucky.
sentences.zh: 他说主教对他说：哦，你很幸运。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And James said, why do you say that?
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯说：你为什么这么说？

sentences.en: And he said, well, it's usually much more than that.
sentences.zh: 主教说：嗯，通常要多得多。

sentences.en: And then he said that that bishop never investigated, never asked him about it again.
sentences.zh: 然后他说那位主教从未进行调查，也再也没有问过他这件事。

sentences.en: He said the bishop did help him with one thing, made sure that he got into some treatment that he said helped him.
sentences.zh: 他说主教确实在一件事上帮了他，确保他接受了一些他所说对他有帮助的治疗。

sentences.en: He said maybe even saved his life.
sentences.zh: 他说甚至可能救了他的命。

sentences.en: But, you know, reported or prosecuted or turned into priest?
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，上报、起诉或把神父移交给司法机关吗？

sentences.en: No, you know, that didn't happen.
sentences.zh: 不，你知道的，那并没有发生。

sentences.en: That really floored me.
sentences.zh: 这真的把我彻底击垮了。

sentences.en: You were lucky.
sentences.zh: 我很幸运。

sentences.en: You were only abused 15 times.
sentences.zh: 我只被虐待了 15 次。

sentences.en: So knowing that the Catholic Church has responded in these ways to this abuse for so long, how did the church respond to this particular report from Pennsylvania?
sentences.zh: 因此，既然知道天主教教会长期以来一直以这些方式回应这种虐待，教会对宾夕法尼亚州的这份特定报告作何回应？

sentences.en: I'd say in two almost contradictory ways.
sentences.zh: 我想说有两种近乎矛盾的回应方式。

sentences.en: On the one hand, they were contrite.
sentences.zh: 一方面，他们感到悔罪。

sentences.en: Let me say that in the name of the Church of Pittsburgh, and in my own name, and in the name of my predecessors, we are sorry.
sentences.zh: 请允许我以匹兹堡教会的名义、以我自己的名义、以及以我的前任们的名义说：我们很抱歉。

sentences.en: I am sorry.
sentences.zh: 我很抱歉。

sentences.en: Some of the bishops in Pennsylvania were very apologetic, but others were more combative, that this is a report about a church that doesn't exist anymore.
sentences.zh: 宾夕法尼亚州的一些主教非常抱歉，但另一些主教则更具好斗性，认为这是一份关于一个已经不复存在的教会的报告。

sentences.en: We've turned the page.
sentences.zh: 我们已经翻开新的一页了。

sentences.en: Why don't we get any credit for how things have looked since 2002?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们自 2002 年以来的表现没有得到任何认可？

sentences.en: And in fact, the Pittsburgh bishop, David Zubik, really gave voice to that.
sentences.zh: 事实上，匹兹堡主教大卫·祖比克确实表达了这一点。

sentences.en: I mean, he said...
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他说……

sentences.en: There was no cover-up going on.
sentences.zh: 根本没有发生任何隐瞒。

sentences.en: And I think that it's important to be able to state that we have, over the course of the last 30 years for sure, been transparent about everything that has, in fact,
sentences.zh: 我认为重要的是能够说明，在过去 30 年的时间里，我们对实际上发生的每一件事都是公开透明的。

sentences.en: been transpiring.
sentences.zh: 在逐渐公开。

sentences.en: So I think that point needs to be made.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得有必要强调这一点。

sentences.en: We've been transparent about everything.
sentences.zh: 我们在所有事情上都保持了透明。

sentences.en: Now, that's actually contradicted in the report, that they've been transparent about everything.
sentences.zh: 然而，报告中的内容实际上与“他们在所有事情上都保持透明”这一说法相矛盾。

sentences.en: But there is the sense among the current class of bishops that we handled this, we have reformed, and we're not getting any credit for it.
sentences.zh: 但现任的主教群体有一种感觉，即我们已经处理了这件事，我们已经进行了改革，但我们没有因此得到任何认可。

sentences.en: Over the last several months, an intense legal battle has played out between my office and individuals who have concealed their identities through sealed court filings.
sentences.zh: 在过去的几个月里，我的办公室与通过密封法院文件隐瞒身份的个人之间展开了一场激烈的法律斗争。

sentences.en: Lord, I listened to the attorney general of Pennsylvania talk about this grand jury report.
sentences.zh: 天哪，我听了宾夕法尼亚州总检察长谈论这份大陪审团报告。

sentences.en: And what he seemed to be saying was, even if the church has reformed, they didn't make this investigation very easy to conduct.
sentences.zh: 他似乎在说，即使教会已经进行了改革，他们也没有让这项调查变得很容易进行。

sentences.en: These petitioners, and for a time, some of the diocese, sought to prevent the entire report from ever seeing the light of day.
sentences.zh: 这些请愿人，以及在一段时间内的某些教区，曾试图阻止整份报告见天日。

sentences.en: Documents were withheld.
sentences.zh: 文件被扣留了。

sentences.en: There was resistance.
sentences.zh: 存在阻力。

sentences.en: So what does that say about whether this is really old news?
sentences.zh: 那么这说明了这是否真的已经是旧闻呢？

sentences.en: He said...
sentences.zh: 他说……

sentences.en: In effect, they wanted to cover up the cover-up.
sentences.zh: 实际上，他们想要掩盖掩盖行为。

sentences.en: There was an attempted cover-up of the cover-up.
sentences.zh: 存在企图掩盖掩盖行为的举动。

sentences.en: And what he's referring to is that two of the dioceses, Harrisburg and Greensburg, attempted to quash the grand jury process.
sentences.zh: 他指的是两个教区——哈里斯堡和格林斯堡——试图阻止大陪审团的程序。

sentences.en: They said, why don't we just let local district attorneys handle this, knowing full well that the attorney general was going to bring more firepower to it, more attention,
sentences.zh: 他们说，为什么不让当地的地方检察官来处理这件事呢？他们心里很清楚，总检察长会为之投入更多火力、更多关注，

sentences.en: more investigative power.
sentences.zh: 更多的调查力量。

sentences.en: Then a number of people who were named in the report, about two dozen or 30 people or so, petitioned the court to prevent the report from being released.
sentences.zh: 接着，报告中点名的一些人，大约有二十多或三十人左右，向法院提起请愿，以阻止报告的发布。

sentences.en: Priests.
sentences.zh: 神父。

sentences.en: They were priests.
sentences.zh: 他们是神父。

sentences.en: They may also have been bishops.
sentences.zh: 他们也可能是主教。

sentences.en: We know at least of one retired bishop who was among the petitioners.
sentences.zh: 我们知道至少有一位退休主教在请愿人之中。

sentences.en: So what ended up happening was the court said, okay, we'll release the report and we'll redact some names.
sentences.zh: 所以最终发生的情况是，法院说，好吧，我们会发布报告，并对一些名字进行涂黑处理。

sentences.en: So when you look at this report, there's plenty of, you know, blackout on this report.
sentences.zh: 所以当你查看这份报告时，你会发现报告上有大量的，你知道的，涂黑的地方。

sentences.en: Sometimes it's names, sometimes it's whole pages.
sentences.zh: 有时是名字，有时是整页。

sentences.en: However, if some of these people had had their way, the report wouldn't have been released at all.
sentences.zh: 然而，如果其中的某些人得逞的话，这份报告根本就不会公之于众。

sentences.en: So while the actual abuse inside the church has been addressed in the 16 years since that first reporting in Boston,
sentences.zh: 因此，虽然自16年前波士顿首次报道以来，教会内部的实际虐待问题已经得到了解决，

sentences.en: it sounds like this attorney general is saying that the attitude of the church is still one of concealing.
sentences.zh: 听起来这位总检察长是在说，教会的态度仍然是隐瞒。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I am not sure I agree with the premise of that question.
sentences.zh: 而且我不确定我是否同意那个问题的前提。

sentences.en: What do you mean?
sentences.zh: 你是什么意思？

sentences.en: I don't think all the abuse has been addressed in the church.
sentences.zh: 我认为教会中的所有虐待行为并没有全部得到解决。

sentences.en: You still hear of fresh cases.
sentences.zh: 你仍然会听到新的案件。

sentences.en: Every year there are still a few cases that are new.
sentences.zh: 每年仍然有少数新案件。

sentences.en: So it's not all cover-ups of old abuse.
sentences.zh: 所以这些并不全是对旧虐待行为的掩盖。

sentences.en: So I hope I didn't leave the impression that it's solved.
sentences.zh: 所以我希望我没有给人留下问题已经解决的印象。

sentences.en: But if most of the abuses did happen years ago, why has it been 16 years since the reporting in Boston?
sentences.zh: 但如果大部分虐待确实发生在多年前，为什么距离波士顿的报道已经过去了16年？

sentences.en: And this investigation in Pennsylvania is only now coming out in 2018.
sentences.zh: 而宾夕法尼亚州的这项调查直到现在2018年才公之于众？

sentences.en: To do an investigation like this, it takes two things.
sentences.zh: 要做这样一项调查，需要两件事。

sentences.en: It takes survivors willing to come forward.
sentences.zh: 需要愿意站出来的幸存者。

sentences.en: And sometimes that can take years.
sentences.zh: 有时这可能需要数年时间。

sentences.en: One of the people who gave testimony about his abuse as a child before the grand jury was 80 years old.
sentences.zh: 在大陪审团面前作证讲述自己童年遭受虐待的一位人士当时已经80岁了。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: It is not uncommon for people in their 40s, 50s, 60s to finally decide to speak.
sentences.zh: 40多岁、50多岁、60多岁的人最终决定开口，这并不罕见。

sentences.en: So that's the first ingredient.
sentences.zh: 所以这是第一个要素。

sentences.en: But second of all, you need, in this case, an attorney general or a district attorney willing to take on the church.
sentences.zh: 但其次，在这个案例中，你需要一个愿意与教会对抗的总检察长或地方检察官。

sentences.en: And willing to put up with the resistance that they're going to get.
sentences.zh: 并且愿意忍受他们将会遇到的阻力。

sentences.en: And you've had that in Pennsylvania.
sentences.zh: 而你在宾夕法尼亚州就遇到了这种情况。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So in Boston, it was the Globe that was willing to take this on.
sentences.zh: 所以在波士顿，是《环球报》愿意承担这件事。

sentences.en: In this case, it sounds like it was the attorney general.
sentences.zh: 在这个案例中，听起来是总检察长。

sentences.en: And their commitment to the story, it sounds like, helped encourage people to come forward.
sentences.zh: 听起来，他们对这篇报道的坚定承诺帮助鼓励了人们站出来。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I guess I just wonder, as someone who's covered this story for years, as you have, what are you thinking about this week with what's come to light in this Pennsylvania report?
sentences.zh: 我想我只是在想，作为一个报道这个故事多年的人，正如你所做的那样，对于本周宾夕法尼亚州这份报告中曝光的内容，你有什么看法？

sentences.en: Well, I think what hasn't really been grappled with adequately by the church or by law enforcement is the systemic nature of this.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为教会或执法部门尚未充分应对的是这个问题的系统性本质。

sentences.en: The case of Cardinal McCarrick in Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: 华盛顿特区的麦卡里克红衣主教案

sentences.en: is one of the keys to that.
sentences.zh: 就是其中的关键之一。

sentences.en: Here you have a cardinal who was accused of sexually abusing adult seminarians or his own younger priests.
sentences.zh: 在这里，你有一位红衣主教，他被指控性虐待成年神学院学员或他自己的年轻神父。

sentences.en: Supposedly, there were people in the church who knew that.
sentences.zh: 据推测，教会里有人知道这一点。

sentences.en: Now, there are people who have studied the church who say that situations like that, which are more widespread than are known.
sentences.zh: 现在，有一些研究教会的人说，类似的情况比人们所知道的要更为普遍。

sentences.en: Bishops who are violating vows of celibacy, priests violating vows of celibacy with adults, with men, with women, and kind of a secret sexual culture.
sentences.zh: 主教违反独身誓言，神父与成年人、男性、女性违反独身誓言，这是一种秘密的性文化。

sentences.en: When you have a culture like that, they say that if there is a priest who's abusing a child and it becomes known,
sentences.zh: 当你拥有这样一种文化时，他们说，如果有一个神父虐待儿童并且事情败露，

sentences.en: that priest can use the knowledge of other people violating their vows of celibacy as blackmail.
sentences.zh: 那个神父就可以利用其他人违反独身誓言的把柄作为勒索手段。

sentences.en: And this is why it never comes out.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么这件事永远不会曝光的原因。

sentences.en: There is a culture of secrecy, a whole culture of cover-up in the church.
sentences.zh: 教会中存在着一种保密文化，一整套掩盖文化。

sentences.en: Ah, so in other words, the problem is that because of the very nature of the church, including celibacy and hierarchy,
sentences.zh: 啊，换句话说，问题在于，由于教会本身的性质，包括独身制度和等级制度，

sentences.en: that this becomes a self-reinforcing system where people can use the knowledge of others' abuse and leadership to protect themselves from repercussions.
sentences.zh: 这变成了一个自我强化的系统，人们可以利用他人虐待和领导层的把柄来保护自己免受惩罚。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And I can hear you responding to this like it is a revelation.
sentences.zh: 我能听出来你对这件事的反应就像听到什么重大揭秘一样。

sentences.en: There are Catholics who study the church and study the sexuality of the priesthood who have been saying this for 20 and 30 years.
sentences.zh: 有些天主教徒研究教会以及神职人员的性取向，他们已经这样说了20年和30年。

sentences.en: Now, along comes this grand jury report, which is dropping in a climate where people are beginning to ask these questions about the church.
sentences.zh: 现在，这份大陪审团报告出炉了，它正诞生于人们开始对教会提出这些疑问的氛围之中。

sentences.en: How can we unravel these interlocking problems?
sentences.zh: 我们如何才能解开这些错综复杂的问题？

sentences.en: And so that's the new stage that we are at and that this report now plays into and why it's not simply retread of things we already know.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我们所处的新阶段，也是这份报告现在所发挥作用的地方，这就是为什么它不仅仅是对我们已知事物的陈词滥调。

sentences.en: It's contributing to the larger picture that people are beginning to look at.
sentences.zh: 它正在为人们开始审视的更大图景做出贡献。

sentences.en: Is part of the discussion that this is prompting about whether or not the church needs to fundamentally re-evaluate the rules around sexuality in the church?
sentences.zh: 这场讨论正在引发的一个问题是，教会是否需要根本性地重新评估教会中关于性取向的规则？

sentences.en: The fact that institutionally it's asked people to not be sexual?
sentences.zh: 从体制上要求人们不谈性欲这一事实？

sentences.en: They've been pressing these questions for a while.
sentences.zh: 他们一直在推动这些问题一段时间了。

sentences.en: The questions about how celibacy, priesthood of men who can't marry, who can't have physical relationships, how that plays into this sexual abuse scandal.
sentences.zh: 关于独身制度、不能结婚、不能有亲密关系的主权男性神职人员，如何卷入这场性虐待丑闻的问题。

sentences.en: The church has been turning away those questions, has said those are not relevant.
sentences.zh: 教会一直在迴避这些问题，并表示这些与此无关。

sentences.en: That's not what we need to look at.
sentences.zh: 这不是我们需要关注的。

sentences.en: But the people calling for that to be examined, that's getting louder now than I've ever heard it before.
sentences.zh: 但那些呼吁审查这一点的人的声音，现在比我以前听到的任何时候都要响亮。

sentences.en: Lori, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 洛里，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们对此表示感谢。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me on.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我参加。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·荣森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收看《重构者》，这是一档完全关于设计之爱及其周围文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you.
sentences.zh: 甚至早在黑胶唱片时代我在夜总会当DJ的时候，你每天晚上都要带着300件你最珍视的宝贝去上班。

sentences.en: And you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你把一个DJ台变成了一个充满美丽50年历史文物的活生生的快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听来自爱彼的《重构者》。

sentences.en: Subscribe to The New York Times, download the Times app today, and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 订阅《纽约时报》，立即下载时报应用程序，即可免费访问30天。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他内容。

sentences.en: Good afternoon.
sentences.zh: 下午好。

sentences.en: Good afternoon.
sentences.zh: 下午好。

sentences.en: I'd like to begin by reading a statement from the president.
sentences.zh: 我想首先宣读一份总统的声明。

sentences.en: As the head of the executive branch and commander-in-chief, I have a unique constitutional responsibility to protect the nation's classified information,
sentences.zh: 作为行政部门首脑和三军统帅，我肩负着一项独特的宪法责任，即保护国家的机密信息，

sentences.en: including by controlling access to it.
sentences.zh: 包括通过控制对其的访问权限。

sentences.en: On Wednesday, President Trump revoked the security clearance of former CIA director John Brennan, who has emerged as a forceful critic of the president's policies and temperament.
sentences.zh: 周三，特朗普总统撤销了前中央情报局局长约翰·布伦南的安全许可，布伦南一直是总统政策和性格的强硬批评者。

sentences.en: He is feeding and fueling hatred and animosity and misunderstandings among Americans.
sentences.zh: 他在助长、煽动美国人之间的仇恨、敌意和误解。

sentences.en: During a briefing at the White House,
sentences.zh: 在白宫的一次简报会上，

sentences.en: Press Secretary Sarah Huckabee Sanders made clear that it was Brennan's negative comments about Trump that motivated the decision to take away his security clearance,
sentences.zh: 白宫新闻秘书莎拉·赫卡比·桑德斯明确表示，正是布伦南对特朗普的负面评论促成了剥夺其安全许可的决定，

sentences.en: which retired officials are allowed to keep so that they can advise their successors.
sentences.zh: 退休官员原本被允许保留这一许可，以便他们能够向继任者提供建议。

sentences.en: Mr. Brennan's line and recent conduct, characterized by increasingly frenzied commentary,
sentences.zh: 布伦南先生的言行以及近期的表现，以日益狂热的评论为特征，

sentences.en: is wholly inconsistent with access to the nation's most closely held secrets and facilities, the very aim of our adversaries, which is to sow division and chaos.
sentences.zh: 与接触国家机密程度最高的信息和设施完全不符，而这正是我们对手的目标——散布分裂与混乱。

sentences.en: On Wednesday afternoon, Brennan responded to the decision on MSNBC.
sentences.zh: 周三下午，布伦南在MSNBC上对这一决定作出了回应。

sentences.en: I do believe that Mr. Trump decided to take this action, as he's done with others, to try to intimidate and suppress any criticism of him or his administration.
sentences.zh: 我确实相信，特朗普先生做出这一决定，就像他对其他人所做的那样，是为了恐吓并压制任何针对他或他政府的批评。

sentences.en: And revoking my security clearances is his way of trying to get back at me.
sentences.zh: 而撤销我的安全许可，是他试图对我进行报复的方式。

sentences.en: But this is not going to deter me at all.
sentences.zh: 但这根本无法阻止我。

sentences.en: I'm going to continue to speak out.
sentences.zh: 我将继续发声。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是今天的《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine, until this summer, when elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受到严密控制的机器在运转，直到今年夏天，选举迎来了群自称改革派的人士。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 自那以后，该党一直陷入一场残酷、混乱且有时令人兴奋的争斗之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在由我和萨拉·科尼格主持的最新一期《地铁》节目中，我们将讲述人们试图维持其影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。
